answer: For an intriguing and thoughtful dinner party, you could invite figures like Benjamin Franklin, Eleanor Roosevelt, and Leonardo da Vinci. Franklin was a polymath, entrepreneur, and diplomat who played a key role in the founding of the United States. Roosevelt was a pivotal political leader who championed civil rights and served as the first female First Lady. Da Vinci, on the other hand, was an extraordinary genius whose contributions to art, science, and technology have had a lasting impact on the world. Their conversations would likely offer contrasting perspectives on innovation, leadership, and societal change.
